abstract:
Each time the series repairs a failure of division it adds a pair of new directions, and repeating the step builds a tower of ever larger algebras. [[t]]

Each floor is the ground algebra with matrix entries, $\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q))$, so nothing essentially new appears. [[c:tower.commuting-copies]] Every floor keeps the ground floor's type, so the clock $d = p - q \bmod 8$ does not advance. [[c:tower.rigidity-clock-frozen]]

What grows is quantum capacity: each rung adds exactly one fermionic mode. [[c:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity]] In the infinite limit, for even charge, the tower becomes the algebra of a free fermion field. [[c:tower.car-limit-even-charge]] The walk ends with the ways our spacetime algebra can be extended by a single direction. [[t]]
introduction: The walk starts with the shape of a single floor, then climbs rung by rung, counting what each step adds, and ends at the infinite limit and a side branch. [[t]] Each result appears after the ones it rests on. [[t]]
i:tower: This section climbs the tower one rung at a time. [[t]]
t:^>tower.commuting-copies:
The tower is built by adding, again and again, a hyperbolic plane: one new positive and one new negative direction. [[t]]

After $k$ rungs the plane generators give real matrices and a twisted copy of the ground generators commutes with them, so \[ \Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \] the ground algebra with matrix entries. [[c:tower.commuting-copies]] Climbing enlarges the algebra without changing its character. [[c:tower.commuting-copies]]
t:tower.commuting-copies>tower.rigidity-:
Because each floor is the ground algebra with matrix entries, its structural features survive the climb. [[c:tower.rigidity-clock-frozen]]

The charge $d = p - q \bmod 8$, the centre, the division ring and the kinds of obstruction are the same on every floor. [[c:tower.rigidity-clock-frozen]] For spacetime every floor is \[ \Cl(1{+}k, 3{+}k) \cong \Mat_{2^{k+1}}(\HH) \] so the clock stays frozen at position $6$. [[c:tower.rigidity-clock-frozen]]
t:tower.rigidity-clock-frozen>tower.ladd:
If the type never changes, the natural question is what the climb does add. [[t]]

The null pairs $v_i, w_i$ adjoined at the rungs obey exactly the canonical anticommutation relations of fermionic modes, \[ v_i v_j + v_j v_i = 0, \qquad w_i w_j + w_j w_i = 0, \qquad v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij} \] as vectors, with no representation chosen. [[c:tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors]] A new rung adds one mode without disturbing the earlier ones. [[c:tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors]]
t:tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors:
Fermionic modes need a space of states to act on. [[t]]

The $v_j$ act by wedging and the $w_j$ by contraction on the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$ of dimension $2^k$, a Fock space whose vacuum $1$ is killed by every $w_j$. [[c:tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung]] Each rung doubles it, \[ \Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1} \] one qubit per rung. [[c:tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung]]
t:tower.fock-module-one-qubit-per-rung>t:
One can then ask how many fermionic modes an algebra can hold at most, using only its own vectors. [[t]]

The answer is the Witt index, \[ \min(p,q) \] the smaller of the counts of positive and negative directions. [[c:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity]] Along the tower it is $\min(p,q) + k$, so each rung adds exactly one mode and no more. [[c:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity]]
t:tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity>towe:
Having counted rung by rung, the walk now lets the tower run forever. [[t]]

When $p - q$ is even the algebraic union has a clean form, \[ \varinjlim T_k \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^\infty} \] the ground algebra with entries in an infinite matrix algebra built by repeated doubling. [[c:tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge]] Equivalently, it is the Clifford algebra of $\R^{p,q}$ with all the planes added at once. [[c:tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge]]
t:tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge>towe:
The algebraic union still has to be completed, with complex scalars and a norm. [[t]]

For even charge the completed limit is \[ \Cl(p,q)_\C \,\otimes\, \CAR \] the ground algebra with the CAR algebra, the standard algebra of a free fermion field with countably many modes. [[c:tower.car-limit-even-charge]] The null vectors added at each rung act directly as that field's creation and annihilation operators, with $w_j = v_j^*$. [[c:tower.car-limit-even-charge]]
t:tower.car-limit-even-charge>tower.answ:
These results answer the question that started the tower: how many times must the completion step be repeated? [[t]]

Under the tameness premise, for a compact wall with a trivial radical line bundle, one ascent completes the physical side, and further rungs arise only beyond it, one per shadow wall. [[c:tower.answers-iteration-question]]

The repetitions never change the algebra's type, and in the even-charge limit they add the modes of a free fermion field. [[c:tower.answers-iteration-question]]
t:tower.answers-iteration-question>scram:
The unit the tower adds turns up elsewhere in the series under other names. [[t]]

A ladder pair $(v_i, w_i)$, a fermionic mode and a unit of Witt-index capacity are one object: a single qubit, of maximal entropy $\ln 2$ nats. [[c:scrambling.pair-mode-qubit-one-object]] The conformal algebra $\Cl(2,4)$ carries exactly two of them, whether one counts pairs or modes. [[c:scrambling.pair-mode-qubit-one-object]]
t:scrambling.pair-mode-qubit-one-object>:
So far each step added two directions at once, and adding a single direction instead leads off the main tower. [[t]]

Our spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ and its mirror $\Cl(3,1)$ can each be extended by one time or one space direction, giving $\Cl(1,4)$, $\Cl(2,3)$, $\Cl(3,2)$ and $\Cl(4,1)$. [[c:odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair]] A space direction doubles, as in $\Cl(1,4) = \Cl(1,3) \oplus \Cl(1,3)$, a time direction complexifies, and the four land on the residues $5$, $7$, $1$ and $3$. [[c:odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair]]
conclusion:
The tower never changes an algebra's type, yet each rung contributes exactly one fermionic mode, and for even charge the infinite climb yields a free fermion field. [[c:tower.car-limit-even-charge]]

The account of when further rungs are needed rests on the tameness assumption listed under what we assume. [[c:tower.answers-iteration-question]] That premise is the only assumption this trail lists. [[t]]
